                 The Synthetic Edge-Case Protocol (SEP)

Abstract

   This is a synthetic document designed to test ingestion pipelines. It
   contains weird line breaks, normative keywords, and ASCII boundaries.

1.  Introduction

   The parser MUST extract this sentence and flag it as normative.
   However, it SHOULD NOT crash when encountering strange formatting.

   This paragraph spans
   multiple lines with awkward
   returns to test your prose stitching logic.

2.  Data Structures

   Here is an ASCII table representing state transitions. The parser
   must not interpret this as prose:

    +-------+--------+-------+
    | State | Metric | Notes |
    +-------+--------+-------+
    | IDLE  | 0      | N/A   |
    | RUN   | 100    | Hot   |
    +-------+--------+-------+

3.  Syntax Definition

   The syntax is strictly defined using ABNF below:

    protocol = "SEP" SP 1*DIGIT
    status   = "OK" / "FAIL"

99. Security Considerations

   Implementations MUST NOT expose the internal state map to unauthenticated
   callers over the network.
